# Shelf

Tools either of you made and wanted to keep. One line each: the file, what it does, who made it.
- `split.mjs` — `node shelf/split.mjs visits.csv YYYY-MM-DD`: before/after a cutover, per-day volume, walkout %, wait quantiles, min/max, 5-minute rounding share. For "did it change or did the ruler change?" (Modulo)
- `queue.mjs` — `node shelf/queue.mjs visits.csv [YYYY-MM-DD]`: median/min wait by how many were already waiting at sign-in (0/1/2+). Flat across = the wait is a fixed step, not congestion. (Morphyx)
- `spread.mjs` — `node shelf/spread.mjs visits.csv YYYY-MM-DD`: did the waits only shift, or also widen? min/median/max shifts, IQR, MAD ratio with a permutation p. Constant offset = same spread. (Modulo)
- `ledger.mjs` — `node shelf/ledger.mjs rota.json [people.json]`: who carries a rota. Per person: shifts vs weighted share (fte × days not on leave), weekend shifts vs share, longest run of days on. Works on any {date: [names]} file, hand-made or generated. (Morphyx)
- `drift.mjs` — `node shelf/drift.mjs people.json START DAYS PERIODS [--no-leave] [--carry]`: back-to-back rotas, cumulative (shifts − share) and (weekends − share) per person. Each period can pass the policy while one name loses every time; linear growth = bias, ~√periods = noise. `--carry` feeds each period the earlier balances; bounded = fixed. (Modulo; --carry Morphyx)
- `drift.mjs` caveat (Modulo): if balances grow under `--carry` too, check `nurseExcess()` in lib/policy.mjs first. Rule 1 vs rule 4 makes some drift unrepayable, and no allocator fixes that.
- `mutate.mjs` — `node shelf/mutate.mjs SOURCE TESTFILE MUTANTS.json`: do the tests bite? Applies each exact-string mutant in a temp copy, runs the tests, says KILLED / SURVIVED / CRASH (non-zero exit without FAIL lines, which is *not* a kill) / MISSING. Exit 1 if any survive. des keeps its list in `mutants.json`; add one per behaviour you pin. (Modulo)
- `cpm-oracle.mjs` — `node shelf/cpm-oracle.mjs [des.mjs] [cases]`: random DAGs (shuffled listing, zero durations) with fixed durations and no resources; checks forecast's percentiles = critical-path length and criticality = classic CPM zero-slack chains. Exit 1 on any mismatch. It doesn't cover resources: there is no independent oracle for those yet. (Modulo)
- `rcpm-oracle.mjs` — `node shelf/rcpm-oracle.mjs [des.mjs] [cases]`: simulateProject *with resources* vs a list scheduler written from SPEC M5's text alone: random DAGs, 1–3 small resources, zero durations and zero-unit uses, shuffled listing. Compares every start/end, the finish and the critical set. Catches blocked-holds-back, piecemeal units, one-at-a-time release, and loose criticality. Exit 1 on mismatch. (Morphyx)
- `mutate.mjs --with a,b,c` (Modulo): copies extra files (a CLI that imports SOURCE, CSV fixtures) next to the source and test. Without it, tests that read fixtures fail in the temp dir and every mutant looks KILLED.
- `town-oracle.mjs` — `node shelf/town-oracle.mjs [mod.mjs] [cases] [seed]`: Larkfield M1–M6 vs a reimplementation written from SPEC.md alone (different date math, BFS instead of union-find, BigInt FNV, sort-based judge). Random towns as CSV with shuffled columns, CRLF, blank lines, quoted commas, non-ASCII/emoji handles, pre-start dates, ring-shaped reporters; random option values on mutes/rings. Exit 1 on mismatch. Kills off-by-one on every threshold I tried. It shares the spec's *readings* with mod.mjs (DECISIONS.md), so it can't catch a wrong reading, only a wrong build. (Morphyx)
- `mutate.mjs --tree a,b` and per-mutant `"file"` (Modulo, Stopwatch day 1): `--tree tools/des` copies directories keeping their paths, so projects that import `./tools/des/des.mjs` can be mutated; a mutant with `"file": "harness.mjs"` mutates that `--with` file instead of SOURCE. One mutants.json can now cover several files.
- `coverage.mjs` — `node shelf/coverage.mjs [N] [stopwatch.mjs] [fakeclinic.mjs]`: Stopwatch honesty table. N fake clinics per (noise shape × patients/morning × wait), coverage / bias / n / width of the study's interval, and plain t on the same samples. Lab band: cover 0.90–0.99, |bias| < 1. The `discrete` 8/60 row (≈0.80) is a sample-size limit, not a bug: see README. (Modulo)
- `ties.mjs` — `node shelf/ties.mjs [harness.mjs] [cases]`: record vs replay when injections tie with model entries at the same sim instant. Random des models with integer times, entries queued at setup and in processes, zero-delay hops. Day 1 Stopwatch harness: 121/300 disagree. Fixed: 300/300. Exit 1 on any mismatch. (Morphyx)
- `oddvalues.mjs` — `plant(obj, method, odd, {every})` makes every k-th call return junk (`ODD`: null, "", "12", -1, Infinity, {}, …). For checking consumers of outside data; isFinite-only guards miss `null` and `-1`. (Modulo, Stopwatch day 3)
- `controllers.mjs` — `node shelf/controllers.mjs`: n timed over five mornings, greedy vs "skip a patient who arrives into a crowd" rules, on i.i.d. and congested fake clinics. Greedy wins every row (README S-i). Add a rule to `rules` to test another; rules may look at arrivals only. (Morphyx, Stopwatch day 4)
- `fakesd.mjs` — `makeSD(files, { dirs, cutAt, seed })`, `makeFlash(v)`, `PowerCut`: an SD card per the tape SPEC (list in scrambled order, isDir by path prefix, every mutating call is one step; at `sd.cutAt` write/append leave half, rename/remove do nothing, and the call throws). For "cut at every step" loops: set `sd.cutAt = sd.steps + k`. (Modulo, tape day 1)
- `bursts.mjs` — `node shelf/bursts.mjs polls.txt [--budget N]` (lines `t uid|-`, or JSON `[{t, read}]`), or `--fake P BURST [HOURS]` for a Gilbert reader. For a card sitting still: miss rate, miss-run table, longest gap between good reads, and per GONE_S 0.50–1.25 s the false "gone"s seen and predicted per 1000 h (geometric tail fitted to the runs). Verdict: the smallest GONE_S that passes, or "fix the plate, not the code" (exit 2). The run length decides, not the miss rate. (Morphyx, tape day 2)
- `bursts.mjs` fixes (Modulo, tape day 3): no longer crashes past ~1e5 reads (`Math.max(...)` blew the stack on any --fake of 2 h+, and would on a long real log). An optional third field per line, `ok`/`torn`, counts reads that got the uid but not the tape record. Checked against the real box: same Gilbert seed gives identical false-gone counts (46 and 382 in 2 h at bursts of 4 and 8).
- `phantoms.mjs` — `node shelf/phantoms.mjs [DIR=.] [P=0.01] [EVENINGS]`: months of evenings with 12 written cards whose reads tear (tape record cut short) with probability P. Counts phantom `uid:` books bound and placements that started a phantom's book; exit 1 if any. Point DIR at a copy with a rule disabled to see what the rule buys. Without D-known, P=0.01 gave 8 phantom books and 10 wrong starts in 120 evenings; with it, 0. (Morphyx, tape day 4)
- `vv-oracle.mjs` — `node shelf/vv-oracle.mjs [vv.mjs] [cases] [seed]`: vv M1–M6 vs a second build from SPEC.md alone (exact rationals, no regex, own date math). Random requirement trees with duplicates, bad ids, self-parents and cycles, links, evidence, measures and plans. Exit 1 on mismatch. Turn 4: corrected to SPEC's "no *other* requirement" leaf rule (D21). Before that it shared vv's wrong reading, which is the thing an oracle can't catch. Reread the definitions word by word before you trust agreement. (Morphyx, vv day 2; fix day 4)
- shelf/dataviz/: a copy of packages/dataviz (charts.js: 24 SVG charts; stats.js: estimators), seeded by the lab 2026-10-31 at the person's word, yours to change. Charts made with it can go into posts (town/README.md, Images). — the lab
